record.original_question: Given an argumentation semantics sigma, its signature Sigma_sigma is the collection of all extension sets sigma(F) realizable by some argumentation framework F. Find exact necessary and sufficient characterizations of the signatures for complete semantics, cf2 semantics, and resolution-based grounded semantics.

evidence.quote: Given an argumentation semantics σ, the signature of σ is the set Σσ = {σ(F ) | F is an AF } .
Open Problem 2 What are exact characterizations of Σcom , Σcf2 , Σrbg ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. An argumentation framework (AF) is a pair F = (A, R), where A is a (finite) set of arguments and R ⊆ A × A is an attack relation. For S ⊆ A, S attacks an argument b if (a, b) ∈ R for some a ∈ S, and S defends an argument a if every attacker of a is attacked by some element of S. A set S ⊆ A is conflict-free if there are no a, b ∈ S with (a, b) ∈ R, and admissible if it is conflict-free and defends each of its elements.

An (extension-based) argumentation semantics σ assigns to each AF F a family σ(F) ⊆ 2^A of subsets of A (the σ-extensions of F). The following three semantics are considered.

(i) Complete semantics (com): S ∈ com(F) iff S is admissible and contains every argument that S defends.

(ii) cf2 semantics: Defined by recursion on the strongly connected components (SCCs) of F. If F has a single SCC, then cf2(F) equals the family of maximal conflict-free subsets of A. Otherwise, for each SCC C, one removes from C all arguments attacked by extension-chosen arguments lying outside C, recursively applies cf2 to the induced subframework, and assembles cf2(F) from these recursive choices.

(iii) Resolution-based grounded semantics (rbg): A resolution of F is an AF obtained from F by, for each pair of mutually attacking arguments a, b (i.e. (a,b),(b,a) ∈ R with a ≠ b), removing exactly one of the two attacks; mutual attacks (a,a) are kept. Let grd(F') denote the unique grounded extension of F' (the least fixed point of the characteristic function). Then rbg(F) is the set of ⊆-minimal elements of { grd(F') : F' is a resolution of F }.

Signatures. The signature of σ is
   Σ_σ = { σ(F) : F is an argumentation framework with finitely many arguments },
i.e. the family of all extension-sets realizable by some AF under σ.

Problem. Provide exact necessary and sufficient characterizations, expressed as intrinsic combinatorial conditions on a family S ⊆ 2^U over a finite set U, of membership in each of the signatures Σ_com, Σ_cf2, and Σ_rbg.
artifact.status_search_result: An exact characterization of the signature Σ_com of complete semantics has been obtained by Linsbichler, Spanring, Woltran and colleagues (see "Characterizing Realizability in Abstract Argumentation", arXiv:1603.09545, and related TU Wien technical reports), settling the complete-semantics part of the original open problem. For cf2 and resolution-based grounded semantics, intermediate results (necessary conditions, alternative characterizations of cf2 avoiding recursion, results on conflict-free/naive labellings) have been published, but a fully agreed-upon exact intrinsic characterization of Σ_cf2 and Σ_rbg does not appear to have been established, so these parts remain open or only partially resolved.

status_evidence.title: Characterizing Realizability in Abstract Argumentation
status_evidence.snippet: A characterization of the signature of complete semantics solving a problem left open by recent work on expressiveness of abstract argumentation semantics.
status_evidence.claim: The signature of complete semantics has been exactly characterized.

status_evidence.title: On the limits of expressiveness in abstract argumentation semantics: realizability and signatures
status_evidence.snippet: Necessary and sufficient conditions for extension-sets to be in the signature; nine semantics with nearly complete characterizations.
status_evidence.claim: Multiple signatures have been (nearly) characterized; some semantics remain partially characterized.

status_evidence.title: Characterizing conflict-free and naive labellings—realizability, uniqueness and patterns of redundancy
status_evidence.snippet: Criteria for several semantics deciding whether a set of extensions is in the signature; subset-antichain is necessary but not sufficient for many semantics.
status_evidence.claim: Partial characterization results for related semantics; cf2 and rbg not fully resolved.
